judged_text: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all team members' destination calendars when the organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null), because the optional chain skips the push. A COLLECTIVE team booking whose organizer has no personal destination calendar creates events on none of the team hosts' calendars even though each host configured one; the next editor will not see why hosts' calendars were skipped.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because of the optional chaining, when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` the push is skipped and the collected team members’ destination calendars are never attached to the event. This directly matches the finding: teamDestinationCalendars can be non-empty (built from `users.slice(1)`), yet it will be dropped if the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar.
